Maladaptive Strategies.value: Situations that make me feel strong emotions
I think about how life would have been different if the event had not occurred
Any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try

Negative Appraisals.value: Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation
I have lost my connection to my community and culture
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: Samantha is a 35-year-old African American woman who has been working as a police officer for nearly ten years. Married and deeply involved in her community, Samantha experienced a traumatic sexual assault while on duty six months ago. The event shattered her sense of self and connection to others. The night of the assault was a blur of violence and fear that left Samantha with both physical and emotional scars. She recalls flashes of pain and intense rage when the memory returns-sensations so vivid she can almost feel the bruises again. Yet, there are also significant gaps in her recollection; certain moments remain shrouded in darkness no matter how hard she tries to remember. Since the assault, Samantha has noticed a profound shift within herself. She believes that someone else would not have found themselves in such a situation and feels isolated from her community and culture. These negative appraisals have led her to adopt maladaptive strategies to cope with the overwhelming emotions. She avoids any situations where she might feel strong emotions or experience disagreement, fearing it could trigger intense memories. Her avoidance behaviors have become entrenched over time. For instance, Samantha avoids patrolling certain areas of the city and has pulled back from family gatherings that once brought her joy. Her husband notices how withdrawn she has become, but he struggles to understand the depth of her pain. The physical reminders of the assault make it difficult for Samantha to remain in situations where she feels emotionally vulnerable. Samantha's memories continue to haunt her daily life. At work, a routine patrol can trigger intense flashbacks and physical sensations, leaving her feeling debilitated. She finds herself increasingly preoccupied with how different her life would have been if the assault had not occurred. This counterfactual thinking adds another layer of distress as she contemplates an alternate reality where she remains whole. The weight of these memories has also reinforced her negative beliefs about herself and others. Samantha feels permanently damaged by the experience, further deepening her sense of isolation from both her community and her role as a police officer. Her husband tries to reassure her that she is not alone, but it only intensifies her frustration with herself for feeling this way. Over time, these maladaptive strategies have created significant rifts in Samantha's life. At work, her performance has slipped due to frequent absences and decreased engagement. At home, the strain on her marriage has become evident as she pulls away from her husband and family events. Despite these growing issues, Samantha has been reluctant to seek help, fearing it would make her seem weak or further damage her reputation. What finally brought Samantha to therapy was a series of minor incidents that escalated into a significant confrontation at work. Her captain, noticing her declining performance and emotional withdrawal, insisted she speak with someone. In therapy sessions, Samantha hopes to find a way to reclaim her sense of self and connection to others without being overwhelmed by the memories and negative appraisals that have consumed her life. Her greatest fear is that she will never fully recover from this trauma, yet she also holds onto hope for a future where she can once again feel safe and connected within both her professional and personal worlds.
